name: Malaita Monarch
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A small black-and-white monarch. White below except for black throat and breast.

name: Togian White-eye
rangeDescription: Togian islands (off sulawesi)
description: A small green songbird with a black forehead, a yellow throat, and white underparts except for the base of the undertail, which is also yellow. Note the indistinct, intermittent white eye-ring.

name: Makira Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Large. Light brown above, white with diffuse black streaks below.

name: Ashy-headed Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to ecuador and southern peru (puno)
description: Small, short-billed flycatcher found in the Andes from Venezuela to Peru. Bright yellow below with two pale wingbars.

name: Streak-headed Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Lowlands of new guinea, including salawati (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea), and aru islands (off southwestern new guinea)
description: A medium-sized honeyeater of lowland and foothill forest edge and gardens. Upperparts dark brown and lower parts gray-brown.

name: Plum-headed Finch
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (burdekin river, queensland to about sydney, new south wales)
description: Small brown bird with finely barred front. Brown above, paler and finely barred, below, with with pale spots on the wing and rump, pale-tipped tail, and tiny plum-colored cap (male also has plum-colored chin).

name: Iphis Monarch
rangeDescription: Uahuka (northern marquesas islands)
description: A glossy bluish-black flycatcher with a variable white belly and undertail. Female brown above, pale below, with a pale lower bill.

name: Red-cockaded Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in pine forest of southeastern usa
description: Rare and declining woodpecker found exclusively in open pine woodlands. Boldly patterned black and white; note especially prominent white cheek and barred back.

name: Plain Swift
rangeDescription: Madeira and western canary islands; winters in northern africa
description: Medium-sized swift, very similar to Common Swift, but is noticeably paler, especially against a dark background. Wings are narrower and very pointed and the tail is longer and more deeply forked than Common or Pallid Swifts.

name: Klages's Antwren
rangeDescription: Central amazonian brazil
description: Tiny, compact antwren with a short tail. Males are gray and heavily streaked black.

name: Klaas's Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Widespread sub-saharan africa and bioko
description: A small, greenish cuckoo. The male has plain white underparts and glossy green upperparts; note dark spurs that extend from the head down onto the lower throat, as well as conspicuous white patch behind the eye.

name: Seychelles Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Highland forest of mahé (seychelles)
description: Small compact owl with very small ear tufts that are often invisible. Buff on the underparts and rufous-brown on the back.

name: Large Blue Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern himalayas (northeastern india and bhutan) to northern myanmar; winters southern myanmar and thai-malay peninsula
description: Typical blue flycatcher; male is bright blue above and orange below, while female is grayish-brown above with a light orange suffusion on her pale belly. Breeds in eastern Himalayan foothill forests and winters in more open habitat in lowlands of Thai-Malay peninsula.

name: Broad-tailed Paradise-Whydah
rangeDescription: Northern angola to democratic republic of the congo, southwestern uganda, kenya, and northeastern south africa
description: Lays its eggs in the nests of Orange-winged Pytilia. The distinctive breeding male has a long, broad tail.

name: Chilean Skua
rangeDescription: Coasts of southern chile and southern argentina; ranges north to tropics
description: Rather large, dark, stocky gull-like seabird with big white wing patches (seen in flight). In summer often seen flying over Patagonian steppe or associating with Kelp Gulls at beaches, dumps, river mouths, and lakes near the coast.

name: Tooth-billed Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Humid eastern panama to western colombia (chocó) and northwestern ecuador
description: A distinctive, fairly large hummingbird with a super long bill. Note the streaky throat and breast, and dull green upperparts with a coppery crown.

name: Baikal Teal
rangeDescription: Breeds in northern and eastern siberia; winters japan, korea, and eastern china
description: Males is exquisitely patterned, with an unmistakable green-and-yellow facial pattern, spotted rose-pink breast, and long, drooping scapulars. Female mostly drab brown but with a distinct white spot near the bill base as well as a very weak hint of the male's facial pattern.

name: Black-headed Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Tasmania (except southwestern), and king and flinders islands (bass strait)
description: Small honeyeater with entirely black head. Upperparts olive with white underparts.

name: Española Mockingbird
rangeDescription: Española island and adjacent southeastern galapagos islands
description: Large gray-and-white songbird with a long tail, curved bill, black mask and mustache, and dark blotches on the underparts. Endemic to Galálapagos.

name: Elusive Antpitta
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern peru (ucayali and madre de dios) and adjacent brazil (acre)
description: A well-named local and very uncommonly encountered species that inhabits the floor of dense terra firme forests in western Amazonia. Striking plumage includes olive-brownish upperparts contrasting with paler, boldy streaked underparts.
